  • Find mean, median and mode, and choose the fair one

Data Appreciation · Week 8 · Idea 1

Understand it

Three "averages":

  • Mean = add them up, divide by how many: =AVERAGE(). One huge value drags it.
  • Median = the middle value when sorted: =MEDIAN(). Not moved by one odd value.
  • Mode = the most common: =MODE().

When one value is far from the rest (an outlier), the median describes a typical person better.

Charts answer questions: bar to compare groups, line for change over time, pie only for a few parts of one whole, scatter for whether two things go together. In Sheets: select the table → Insert → Chart → pick the type. A chart someone else can read has a title that says what it shows, labelled axes, the source and the date, and bar charts start at zero.

Data Appreciation · Week 8 · Key words

Key words

Mean / median / mode
the arithmetic average / the middle / the most common
Outlier
a value far from the rest
Axis
the scale along the side or bottom of a chart
Data Appreciation · Week 8 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Work out mean, median and mode for pocket money
  2. Choose the chart for three questions
  3. Make a bar chart with a title, labels and source

Need a hand? Sort the numbers first: the median and mode jump out.

Done early? Find a bar chart whose axis does not start at zero and redraw it honestly.

Data Appreciation · Week 8 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Pocket money (₦): 200, 300, 300, 300, 400, 500, 600, 3000. Which best describes a typical child?
  • Make a bar chart from your table with a title that states the finding, labelled axes, the source and the date.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
